Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-22 08:30 PT / 16:30 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Marcus (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Olivia (Astor Head of Platform), Dante (SRE), Priyanka (Security), Samir (Product)

Summary (auto-gen, may be partial):
- Discovery call focused on reliability, incident tolerance, multi-region routing and fallback policies across Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
- Customer wants deterministic failover behavior, SLA clarity, and proof via benchmarks.
- Next steps: pricing/SLA doc, benchmark plan, security checklist.

Topics: reliability SLAs, multi-region routing, model fallbacks, KV/prefix caching during failover, private/VPC networking, encryption/KMS, audit logs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Marcus: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you doing this - uh - deep dive. quick who do we have, Olivia?
[00:07] Olivia: hi Marcus, thanks. Olivia here, Head of Platform at Astor. we have Dante (SRE), Priyanka from security and Samir from product.
[00:12] Marcus: awesome, thanks. Priya and I will run through our approach to incident tolerance, fallback patterns, and how Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private map to your requirements.
[00:22] Priya: hey all, quick agenda - current architecture, failure modes you care about, what acceptable RTO/RPO looks like, and proposed safeguards.
[00:30] Dante: we typically look for sub-second p95 for our user-facing features, but more importantly deterministic behavior when a region or model becomes unavailable. so the question is how do we avoid silent degradations where latencies spike or responses are stale.
[00:43] Priyanka: and from security we're mostly concerned about keys and logs during failover - e.g., do we leak any telemetry, where are audit logs stored, and if we do private deployment how do we integrate with our HSM/KMS?
[00:54] Marcus: great, that's helpful. quick call-out - we'll reference a couple docs after the call: Dedicated SLA brief, multi-region routing guide, and a benchmark plan.
[01:05] Priya: one more logistics Q - are we expecting to run failover tests with synthetic traffic or will you run a controlled incident on your side?
[01:12] Priya (Redwood): we can help run both. typically we provide a test harness and can also coordinate a simulated regional outage in a sandboxed environment for Dedicated or Private pilots - for Hosted we run controlled throttling and can show routing to fallback model variants.
[01:27] Samir: can you clarify fallback model variants - like do you have smaller/quantized models to drop to? what's the tradeoff?
[01:33] Priya: yes - policy-level fallback is twofold: model variant fallback (e.g., high-capacity -> quantized low-cost model) and region fallback (route to another region or dedicated pool). quality vs latency/cost is the tradeoff; we can auto-apply a degradation policy with explicit SLAs per route.
[01:50] Dante: how deterministic is the routing? if a region is slow, will requests automatically go to another region or queue up and cause client-side timeouts?
[01:58] Priya: routing is policy-driven. we expose SLO monitors in the console - you can set thresholds (latency, error rate, capacity) that trigger routing actions. actions include: failover to a regional pool, swap to a compatible model variant, or queue with backpressure. default for Hosted is to prefer regional routing to another Hosted region, and Dedicated customers can pin to dedicated pools with automatic burst to Hosted if configured.
[02:20] Olivia: we like the idea of automatic failover but we need guarantees. what are the SLA implications if you route to Hosted from Dedicated?
[02:29] Marcus: good question - SLA differs. Dedicated contracts include guaranteed throughput/latency for the reserved pool. if we invoke cross-tier fallback (Dedicated -> Hosted), that path does not carry the Dedicated SLA; we surface that clearly in the console and recommend policies that keep fallbacks for best-effort continuity rather than to meet Dedicated SLA commitments. we'll include language in the SLA doc about cross-tier fallback behavior.
[02:52] Priyanka: what's your typical RPO/RTO in multi-region incidents for Hosted?
[02:57] Priya: Hosted is architected across multiple regions - for region-level outage we have failover mechanisms that typically switch traffic within 30-90s depending on cache warming and KV prefix hits. RTO varies with prefix cache warm-up; we can accelerate with active KV replication at extra cost.
[03:14] Dante: prefix cache warming - can you explain impact? we rely heavily on first-token latency and warm KV cache to serve personalizations.
[03:21] Priya: sure - our runtime caches KV pairs (prefix or session KV) to avoid recomputation. when you move traffic to a new region without replicated KV cache, initial requests hit cold cache and latency spikes. options: active replication (synchronous or async), or route to model variant that tolerates cold cache better. we can instrument per-customer cache warm strategy.
[03:42] Samir: for Dedicated pilots, do we get the ability to pre-warm KV caches across regions?
[03:47] Priya: yes, Dedicated customers can opt into cross-region KV replication or background pre-warming jobs. we'll include the runbook.
[03:53] Olivia: on the security front - if we replicate KV or logs across regions, we need to ensure data residency controls. what are controls around residency and encryption in transit and at rest?
[04:04] Marcus: we support customers selecting region pairs and limiting replication. for Private deployments you control the region entirely. for Hosted/Dedicated we support region scoping and can disable cross-region replication where required. all traffic is TLS, and data at rest is encrypted. we support customer-managed keys (KMS) for Dedicated and Private.
[04:21] Priya: small note - HSM integration for Private is supported; Dedicated customers can bring KMS keys via cloud provider integrations; Hosted supports customer-managed keys for an add-on. details in security docs.
[04:33] Priya (customer): curious about observability during failover - how much fidelity do we get in the console for tracing what happened?
[04:40] Priya (Redwood): our Console provides per-request traces, token-level cost/latency breakdown, and a timeline for routing decisions. for pilots we'd enable verbose tracing so you can see decision points: threshold breach, selected fallback action, and model variant chosen. traces are retained per your retention policy; longer retention is an add-on.
[04:56] Dante: can traces contain PII? we need to ensure logs scrub user text by default.
[05:02] Priya: by default we redact full-request text from logs for Hosted; Dedicated/Private you control retention and whether request bodies are kept. we'll mark recommended defaults in the security checklist.
[05:13] Samir: what's the typical failover latency to another region for a small batch of concurrent requests - say 50 rps?
[05:20] Priya: depends on region distance and caching. rough ballpark: 100-300ms additional network, plus cold-cache penalty which can add 200-800ms if caches are cold. with active replication we see <150ms additional at p95. we'll surface real numbers in the benchmark plan.
[05:38] Olivia: about testing - we want to run an A/B where 10% traffic is routed to fallback for 24 hours to validate quality and cost. can we do that safely?
[05:46] Marcus: yes, we support traffic shaping and can run canary rollouts with automatic rollback if quality regressions are detected. our rollout tool lets you specify percentage, observability hooks, and auto-failback criteria.
[05:58] Priya: also note function/tool calling or structured outputs might behave slightly differently across model variants - we'll help craft a compatibility test harness.
[06:08] Priyanka (Security): one more on compliance - do you have SOC 2 and do you provide audit logs showing routing decisions for a given request?
[06:14] Marcus: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II. we can provide routing decision logs as part of audit logs; for Hosted customers we retain those for a default window and we have options for extended retention.
[06:25] Priyanka (Security): And for Private, logs stay in our environment?
[06:29] Priya: yes, Private keeps logs on customer infra; we can integrate with your SIEM.
[06:34] Dante: are there any failure scenarios where we should not expect a graceful fallback? e.g., global control plane outage?
[06:42] Priya: good question - a full control-plane outage impacts hosted routing decisions; that's why for Dedicated customers we offer a private control plane option or an on-prem agent that can maintain core routing locally. we also recommend client-side fallback logic as last-resort - e.g., short-circuit to a cached response or show degraded experience.
[06:59] Samir: what's the billing model when routing crosses regions or model variants?
[07:04] Marcus: billing is usage-based; if you route from Dedicated to Hosted, you'll see charges aligned to the pool you hit. quantized lower-cost models cost less per token. cross-region egress may apply if we move data between cloud regions - we surface costs in the cost breakdown.
[07:18] Olivia: for procurement, we need a clear SLA table that lists uptime and latency guarantees per product tier and what fails those SLAs - is that something you can share?
[07:27] Marcus: yes, we'll send the SLA brief; it includes uptime commitments, p99 latency targets for Dedicated under normal conditions, and explicit exceptions (force majeure, cross-tier fallback).
[07:37] Priya: ok i'll note that and attach the sample SLA to the follow-up.
[07:41] Priya (Redwood): quick technical deep dive - our runtime measures per-shard capacity and we do smart routing to balance token load. if a specific shard is overloaded we'll route to a compatible shard or model variant.
[07:51] Dante: are shards per-tenant or multi-tenant?
[07:54] Priya: Dedicated shards are single-tenant; Hosted shards are multi-tenant but isolated at process level. we provide capacity reservations to avoid noisy neighbor issues.
[08:02] Olivia: for our pilot we need to mirror production-like traffic including session stickiness; can the pilot replicate sticky sessions across regions?
[08:09] Priya: yes, session stickiness can be enabled and we replicate session metadata; when crossing regions we need to replicate that state (optionally).
[08:18] Samir: do you have any customer stories where multi-region failover was exercised in production?
[08:23] Marcus: yes - a retail customer had a regional outage and our automatic regional routing plus active KV replication avoided a majority of user-visible errors; we'll redact the customer name but include a short case study in follow-up.
[08:35] Priya: one nuance - some enterprise customers prefer cold-standby in a second region to avoid cross-region replication for data residency reasons; that's an option and we can script warm-up procedures.
[08:47] Priyanka (Security): about encryption keys - if we replicate encrypted blobs across regions, are keys replicated or do we re-encrypt per-region?
[08:55] Priya: you can choose: either keys are replicated (managed keys) or we re-encrypt with a region-specific key (customer-managed KMS) to meet residency policies.
[09:05] Dante: at what point do we bring Redwood into our incident playbooks - is there an on-call integration?
[09:10] Marcus: for Dedicated/Private customers we provide SRE escalation paths and can integrate with your PagerDuty/Splunk. Hosted customers have a support tier; enterprise support includes a named TAM and 24/7 escalation.
[09:22] Olivia: last question for now - how do you measure quality regressions during fallback? are there built-in eval hooks?
[09:28] Priya: yes, Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. during canaries we run synthetic prompts and A/B evals; we can auto-roll back if quality drops beyond thresholds.
[09:40] Marcus: ok let's recap and action items. we'll send SLA/pricing, Priya will send benchmark plan and runbook, Olivia will share compliance list, and we'll schedule the follow-up console demo.
[09:51] Olivia: thanks everyone, this was super useful.
[09:53] Priyanka: thanks all.
